problems.title: Remainder from a linear divisor
problems.question: Find the remainder when 4x²+16x+2 is divided by x+4.
problems.idea: Use the appropriate identity or theorem and check all restrictions and possible configurations.
formulas: The remainder theorem gives remainder $P(-4)$.

problems.title: Combine exponents to find a base
problems.question: Find a if a³·(a²)³=2³⁶.
problems.idea: Use the appropriate identity or theorem and check all restrictions and possible configurations.
steps: The equation is a⁹=2³⁶=(2⁴)⁹. The ninth power is strictly increasing on the reals, so a=16.

problems.title: How many nines make a power of nine?
problems.question: Write 9¹⁵ as a sum of equal terms 9. How many terms are needed?
problems.idea: Use the appropriate identity or theorem and check all restrictions and possible configurations.
formulas: Count = total/size of each term.
steps: 9¹⁵/9=9¹⁴=3²⁸.

problems.title: Crossings of a broken line
problems.question: An open polygonal chain T₁T₂…T₁₉₉ meets a line a. What is its maximum number of proper crossings?
problems.idea: Use the appropriate identity or theorem and check all restrictions and possible configurations.
formulas: A chain of 199 vertices has 198 segments; each straight segment can cross a line at most once.
steps: The upper bound is 198. Alternate vertices on opposite sides of a, with distinct crossing locations, to achieve one crossing per segment.

problems.title: A tangential quadrilateral perimeter
problems.question: A quadrilateral has an incircle and consecutive sides 6,7,8. Find its perimeter.
problems.idea: Use the appropriate identity or theorem and check all restrictions and possible configurations.
formulas: In a tangential quadrilateral, opposite-side sums are equal.
steps: If the fourth side is d, 6+8=7+d, so d=7. Perimeter=6+7+8+7=28.

problems.title: Combine two shopping bills
problems.question: Ten notebooks and four pens cost 32.50 GEL; eight notebooks and five pens cost 35 GEL. Find the cost of three notebooks and two pens.
problems.idea: Use the appropriate identity or theorem and check all restrictions and possible configurations.
formulas: Let notebook price be u and pen price v; solve $10u+4v=32.5$, $8u+5v=35$.
steps: Elimination gives u=1.25 GEL and v=5 GEL. Then 3u+2v=3.75+10=13.75 GEL.

problems.title: Square a quotient to obtain a fourth-power sum
problems.question: (a²−b²)/(ab)=6. Find (a⁴+b⁴)/(a²b²).
problems.idea: Use the appropriate identity or theorem and check all restrictions and possible configurations.
steps: The given expression squared is 36, so the required value is 36+2=38. The original condition already requires ab≠0.

problems.title: Bounds for a linear expression
problems.question: −2<m<3 and −1<k<7. Find sharp bounds for L=2m−3k.
problems.idea: Use the appropriate identity or theorem and check all restrictions and possible configurations.
formulas: Multiply inequalities, reversing order when multiplying by a negative.
steps: −4<2m<6 and −21<−3k<3. Adding gives −25<L<9. Both endpoints are excluded and can be approached.

problems.title: Rhombus inradius
problems.question: A rhombus has side 24 and acute angle 30°. Find its inradius.
problems.idea: Use the appropriate identity or theorem and check all restrictions and possible configurations.
formulas: Area $=s^2\sin\alpha=r\cdot2s$, hence $r=s\sin\alpha/2$.

problems.title: A tangent cuts off a corner triangle
problems.question: A right triangle has AB=10,BC=6,AC=8. An additional tangent to its incircle cuts sides AB,AC at M,K. Find perimeter AMK.
problems.idea: Use the appropriate identity or theorem and check all restrictions and possible configurations.
formulas: Equal tangent segments from the same point have equal lengths; semiperimeter of ABC is 12.
steps: The tangent lengths from A to the original contact points are s−BC=12−6=6 on each side.
For the cutting tangent between A and the incircle, its contact point splits MK into the remaining tangent lengths. Hence AM+AK+MK=6+6=12.

problems.title: Forbidden inputs of an absolute-value denominator
problems.question: For how many integer x is 1/(|x−2|−1) undefined?
problems.idea: Use the appropriate identity or theorem and check all restrictions and possible configurations.
formulas: The denominator vanishes when $|x-2|=1$.
steps: The forbidden values are x=1,3, both integers.

problems.title: Cancel a geometric three-term factor
problems.question: Simplify (199³−1)/(199^(−n)+199^(−n−1)+199^(−n−2)).
problems.idea: Use the appropriate identity or theorem and check all restrictions and possible configurations.
steps: Cancel r²+r+1 with r=199. The quotient is (199−1)199^(n+2)=198·199^(n+2).

problems.title: An apparent root is excluded by the domain
problems.question: Count roots of (x−1)/(3x+3)−(x+3)/(x+2)=−2x²/[3(x+1)(x+2)].
problems.idea: Use the appropriate identity or theorem and check all restrictions and possible configurations.
formulas: Domain $x\ne-1,-2$; multiply by the common nonzero denominator.
steps: The equation becomes (x−1)(x+2)−3(x+3)(x+1)=−2x². Simplification gives −11x−11=0.
Its only algebraic candidate is x=−1, excluded by the original denominators. There are no solutions.

problems.title: An incircle in a right trapezoid
problems.question: A right trapezoid has acute angle 30°, midline 15 and an incircle. Find the radius.
problems.idea: Use the appropriate identity or theorem and check all restrictions and possible configurations.
formulas: Height $h=2r$; the slanted leg is $h/\sin30°=2h$; bases sum equals legs sum.
steps: The bases sum to 30. The legs sum to h+2h=3h=6r. Therefore 6r=30 and r=5.

problems.title: A rectangle split by an angle bisector
problems.question: The B-bisector meets side AD at E with DE:EA=1:5. Rectangle perimeter is 154. Find its longer side.
problems.idea: Use the appropriate identity or theorem and check all restrictions and possible configurations.
formulas: The 45° bisector gives $AE=AB$.
steps: Write DE=t,EA=5t. Then AD=6t and AB=5t. Perimeter=2(6t+5t)=22t=154, giving t=7.
The longer side is 6t=42 cm.

problems.title: Integral values of a rational expression
problems.question: For how many positive integers p is 15/(2p−3) an integer?
problems.idea: Use the appropriate identity or theorem and check all restrictions and possible configurations.
formulas: The odd denominator must be a divisor of 15, and $2p-3\ge-1$.
steps: Allowed denominators are −1,1,3,5,15. They correspond to p=1,2,3,4,9.
There are five values; the negative denominator −1 is valid because only p must be positive.

problems.title: Order rational powers
problems.question: Order A=2.5·(3/5)^0, B=(3/5)^(−2), C=(3/7)^(−1), D=5^(−2)/4^(−3).
problems.idea: Use the appropriate identity or theorem and check all restrictions and possible configurations.
formulas: Negative exponents give reciprocals.
steps: Thus C<A<D<B.

problems.title: Domain of a fraction containing fractions
problems.question: Find the sum of excluded inputs of y=(19x−10)/[3/(x−2)−2/(x+1)].
problems.idea: Use the appropriate identity or theorem and check all restrictions and possible configurations.
formulas: First exclude inner-denominator zeros; then exclude zeros of the entire outer denominator.
steps: The inner fractions exclude x=2 and x=−1. Their difference is (x+7)/[(x−2)(x+1)], which vanishes at x=−7.
All three remain excluded in the original expression. Their sum is 2−1−7=−6.

problems.title: A circumradius fixes one side, not the largest side
problems.question: In parallelogram ABCD, B and C bisectors meet at M. The circumradius of BCM is 12. Find the parallelogram’s larger side.
problems.idea: Use the appropriate identity or theorem and check all restrictions and possible configurations.
formulas: Adjacent parallelogram angles are supplementary, so their bisectors are perpendicular; a right triangle has circumradius half its hypotenuse.
steps: BMC=90°, so BC=24. The condition puts no length restriction on AB.
For a rectangle with BC=24, the B and C bisectors always meet 12 from BC. Both AB=30 and AB=40 satisfy all the data, but the larger sides are 30 and 40 respectively.
The only fixed side is BC=24. The maximum of the two side lengths can be any value at least 24.
problems.answer: BC=24; the larger side is not uniquely determined.
problems.note: The question incorrectly treats the fixed side BC as necessarily the larger side. No condition on the other side or the location of M is given.

problems.title: A rhombus with three vertices on a circle
problems.question: A circle centred at one rhombus vertex passes through all three other vertices. Find the ratio of arcs cut by the long diagonal.
problems.idea: Use the appropriate identity or theorem and check all restrictions and possible configurations.
formulas: The circle radius equals a rhombus side and its shorter diagonal.
steps: Let A be the centre. AB=BC=AC makes triangle ABC equilateral, so B=60° and the adjacent angle BAD=120°.
The long diagonal is BD. Its endpoints subtend 120° at centre A, leaving the other arc 240°. Their ratio is 1:2.

problems.title: Simplify a quotient of rational expressions
problems.question: Evaluate [a−4ab/(a+b)+b] ÷ [a/(a+b)−b/(b−a)−2ab/(a²−b²)] at a=199,b=100.
problems.idea: Use the appropriate identity or theorem and check all restrictions and possible configurations.
formulas: The first bracket is $(a-b)^2/(a+b)$; combine the second over $(a-b)(a+b)$.
steps: The second numerator is a(a−b)+b(a+b)−2ab=(a−b)², so that bracket is (a−b)/(a+b).
Division leaves a−b=99. At the given numbers all denominators and the divisor are nonzero.

problems.title: Collect all powers with the same base
problems.question: Simplify a^a b^b c^c a^b b^c c^a a^c b^a c^b, for integers a,b,c wherever the powers are defined.
problems.idea: Use the appropriate identity or theorem and check all restrictions and possible configurations.
formulas: Each base has total exponent $a+b+c$.
steps: Collect the a, b and c factors separately: a^(a+b+c)b^(a+b+c)c^(a+b+c)=(abc)^(a+b+c).
Integer exponent rules apply on the original domain; undefined zero or negative-exponent cases do not become valid by simplification.

problems.title: Count positive integer price combinations
problems.question: How many positive integer ordered pairs (a,b) solve 500a+200b=9000?
problems.idea: Use the appropriate identity or theorem and check all restrictions and possible configurations.
formulas: Divide by 100: $5a+2b=90$.
steps: a must be even, so set a=2k. Then b=45−5k>0 and k≥1. This gives k=1,…,8, exactly eight pairs.

problems.title: Distance to a trapezoid diagonal
problems.question: An isosceles trapezoid has perimeter 100. A diagonal is perpendicular to a leg and makes 30° with a base. Which listed distance from a small-base vertex to that diagonal is possible?
problems.idea: Use the appropriate identity or theorem and check all restrictions and possible configurations.
formulas: Use vertices $A=(0,0),D=(4t,0),B=(t,\sqrt3t),C=(3t,\sqrt3t)$.
steps: These coordinates follow from tan30°=h/(L−t) and perpendicularity t(L−t)=h², which together give L=4t,h=√3t.
The bases are 4t,2t and both legs 2t. Perimeter=10t=100, so t=10.
The distance from B to diagonal AC is twice triangle ABC’s area divided by AC: (2t·√3t)/(2√3t)=t=10. C itself lies on the diagonal and has distance 0; only 10 is listed.
problems.answer: 10 among the choices; the two small-base vertices have distances 10 and 0.

problems.title: Take midpoint quadrilaterals twice
problems.question: ABCD has equal diagonals. Connecting consecutive side midpoints gives MNKP; repeat to get EFGH. Find an angle of EFGH.
problems.idea: Use the appropriate identity or theorem and check all restrictions and possible configurations.
formulas: Varignon’s theorem: midpoint-quadrilateral sides are parallel to and half the original diagonals.
steps: Equal diagonals make MNKP a rhombus. Its diagonals are perpendicular.
The sides of EFGH are parallel to these perpendicular diagonals, making EFGH a rectangle. Every angle is 90°.
